critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1061 — the new avg<=0 guard is placed correctly BEFORE `proceeds = qty * price` in the demo SELL branch. Good.

server.py:920–1010 — the LIVE Binance SELL path does NOT have the same avg_price<=0 guard. If a live-mode bot ever has a stale zero avg_price, it would still book profit=proceeds. Recommend mirroring the guard there too (near line 933 after `qty = quantity or bot.get('position_qty', 0.0)`).

Transactions.jsx:280 — cost <= 0.01 guard is correct, but the fallback also silently hides legit tiny sells. Consider showing '—' or 'N/A' rather than nothing so the row still communicates 'no ROI available' rather than an empty visual gap.

Transactions.jsx:282 — Math.abs(roi) > 500 hides negative outliers too (e.g., a -600% loss). That's a defensive UX choice, but if the app ever books a real >500% loss it will be silently hidden. Consider two-sided threshold like -95 < roi < 500.

rca of the issue: Original bug: some SELL transactions had corrupt data (profit ≈ amount) because the bot doc's avg_price was 0.0 at SELL time, making `profit = proceeds - qty*avg_price = proceeds - 0 = proceeds`, which yielded infinite ROI on the UI. Cause: stale/duplicate bot docs that got their position_qty populated but never had avg_price set. Fix stack: (1) backend refuses to book a SELL when avg_price<=0 and pos_qty>0 (server.py:1061) — verified by direct trade endpoint test returning 400. (2) frontend caps ROI display at ±500% and hides for cost<$0.01 (Transactions.jsx:280–291) — verified visually and programmatically. (3) DB backfill zeroed 12 historical corrupt rows (profit>=95%*amount) with note='reset_stale_avg' — verified: exactly 12 such rows present, total profit correctly recomputed to $94.47. Residual: 3 lesser outlier rows (profit 87–92% of amount → ROI 711–1120%) exist but are hidden by the frontend cap; recommend a stricter secondary backfill.
